name: the language
headline: The *language* of Hypercomb
say: Hypercomb uses a few exact words, and each means one thing. A hive is your own place, kept on your device. A tile is one piece of content. A layer is one moment of a place, kept for good. A signature is the name content gives itself. A bee is a small piece of behaviour that acts when it is needed, or when you say its word. A pheromone is a signed mark of interest left on content, so people with matching interests can find it; carrying it to them is still being built. Replication is how work moves between hives, checked byte by byte. The brood is where code from someone else waits, and never runs, until you accept it. And a colony is a domain with the hives it hosts; there are many, and none of them is in charge.
